surface: Calendar feed and This app storage
observed: Calendar calls the admin-scoped calendar feed-key status route on mount without checking settings permission or recent local-password proof, producing HTTP 403 in an ordinary local-network session.

This app calls the admin-scoped storage route whenever the person has settings permission, but does not check recent local-password proof; its failure is caught by the page-wide error state and can hide otherwise available health information.
Both reads expose status and path metadata rather than secret values, but the server intentionally protects them with the same admin-route assurance policy.
target: Skip each protected read until the current person has the required permission and session assurance.
Show a focused confirmation state with a real link to the existing My account reauthentication form.
Keep calendar browsing, app health, update status, and all confirmed-session feed and storage features working independently.
boundaries: Do not read, log, capture, or expose feed keys, storage response content, tokens, or configuration values.
Frontend only; no API, auth, database, or server changes.
The naming preview POST blocked by the GET-only capture harness is recorded as a harness limitation, not changed as a product defect.
